name: heralded-memory
question: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time did each report?

Q0.label: main
Q0.text: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time did each report?
Q0.keywords: heralded entanglement remote quantum memories experiment rate fidelity storage time

Q1.label: subject
Q1.text: Two spatially separated quantum memory nodes, such as trapped ions, neutral atoms, nitrogen-vacancy centres, rare-earth doped crystals or atomic ensembles, linked to each other by photons.
Q1.keywords: quantum memory nodes trapped ion neutral atom NV centre rare-earth crystal atomic ensemble network node

Q2.label: approach
Q2.text: Heralded entanglement generation between memories by interfering emitted photons and performing a Bell-state measurement at a middle station, using single-photon, two-photon or DLCZ schemes.
Q2.keywords: heralded entanglement Bell-state measurement photon interference single-photon two-photon DLCZ herald station

Q3.label: outcome
Q3.text: The heralding rate or success probability of entanglement, the fidelity of the shared Bell state, and the storage or coherence time of the quantum memories.
Q3.keywords: heralding rate success probability Bell-state fidelity storage time coherence time memory lifetime

Q4.label: context
Q4.text: Memory nodes placed in separate laboratories or buildings and connected by kilometres of optical fibre, often with frequency conversion to telecom wavelengths.
Q4.keywords: separate laboratories buildings kilometres optical fibre telecom wavelength frequency conversion metropolitan link
